scope: PR #15 'Centralize capability templates under registry' (merge 6b3262af on dev). Source touch = crates/oya-dev-cli/src/{foundry_capability_schema_gates.rs, foundry_eval_gates.rs, lib.rs}. Data move = product-control/capabilities/** -> registry/capability-templates/**.

layer_violations.snippet: for entry in fs::read_dir(capabilities_dir) ... let contents = fs::read_to_string(&path) ...
layer_violations.rule_cited: ADR-0056 line 177: 'cli — CLI binary or CLI library (subcommand handlers + optional [[bin]])'. Lines 171-174: kernel owns ports+types, domain owns business logic, application owns use cases. fs::read_dir + YAML parse of capability templates is domain/usecase work, not cli work.
layer_violations.why: The cli crate directly walks the filesystem and parses capability/eval template YAML. Equivalent kernel + domain crates already exist (oya-foundry-capability-registry-kernel, oya-foundry-capability-domain) — confirming the layer split is canonical, not aspirational. The dev-cli gate should depend on those kernels and call a usecase, not re-implement template-loading at the presentation layer.
layer_violations.fix: Introduce/locate an oya-foundry-capability-template-application (or extend an existing usecase crate) that exposes load_capability_records(capabilities_dir) -> Result<Vec<CapabilityRecord>, _>. The cli gate then calls that usecase and only formats output. Keep the path-default flag in cli (presentation), keep the IO + parse in usecase/adapter.

layer_violations.evidence: The IO-in-cli pattern PRE-DATES PR #15. PR #15 only swaps the default string ('product-control/capabilities' -> 'registry/capability-templates') in lib.rs and the two gate files (1-line each, 3 source-line diff total).
layer_violations.why: The architecture violation is the responsibility of the crate's original author, not this PR. PR #15 is a path-rename cleanup. Realist Check: downgrades A4-V1 actionability against this PR to OBSERVED-NOT-INTRODUCED; the merge does not worsen layer adherence. Mitigated by: pre-existing IO scope; PR diff is +3/-3 in source. The finding is logged for the next cleanup wave (LEAN-A series) rather than as a blocker for #15.

consolidation_analysis: PR #15 collapses ONLY a data-plane directory (product-control/capabilities -> registry/capability-templates). It does NOT merge any kernel + adapter crate, does NOT remove any port trait, does NOT erase a usecase boundary. Three .yaml fixtures were renamed; registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json gained 105 rows registering them as control-plane artifacts. No Rust module boundary changed.
adr_check: PR adds zero new ADRs and amends zero existing ADRs. ADR-0056 untouched. ADR-0116 cited as cover, not amended. The deep-dive-oyatie-sst-consolidation.md spec (docs/specs/ + docs/decisions/specs/) shows only a 1-line path edit ('product-control/' removed from a comment); the spec's clean-architecture principle on line 24 ('kernel <- domain <- application <- {adapter, ...}') and the inward-flow diagram on line 75 are unchanged. Inward-flow rule is intact.

spec_coherence.notes: Spec retains kernel<-domain<-app<-adapter direction (line 24, 75). Path edit on line 78 ('registry/      # catalog + capability records' replacing 'registry/, product-control/      # catalog + capability records') is consistent with the data move and does not redefine the SoT layer model. Spec correctly treats registry/ as control-plane data, not code, so layer placement of consumers is unaffected by the move.

realist_check: A4-V1 is genuine architectural drift but the PR itself is a 3-line path swap. Treating #15 as REJECT would penalize a clean topology move for a flaw the merge did not introduce. Treating it as ACCEPT would silently bless the cli-owns-template-IO pattern. Verdict REVISE = accept the path move, file the layer fix as a follow-up gate task (LEAN-A family) so the violation is tracked, not ratified.
verdict_justification: PR is architecturally NEUTRAL on the layer enum (no kernel/adapter collapse, no ADR weakening, spec coherent). Pre-existing IO-in-cli pattern surfaces during review and should be tracked but is not a #15 blocker. REVISE = land the path/registry move + open a follow-up to push capability-template loading down to a usecase that consumes the existing oya-foundry-capability-*-kernel crates.
